scenes.name: Grammys, Óscars, Hall of Fame y el Pulitzer
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.desc: Los grandes premios rechazaron o reconocieron tarde al hip hop. En los Grammy de 1984, la noche de Thriller, Herbie Hancock tocó «Rockit» con Grand Mixer D.ST en los platos: para Paradise Gray, la primera vez que se vio en la tele. En 1989 se creó el Grammy al mejor rap pero se entregó fuera de la retransmisión: Def Jam y Rush encabezaron el boicot y DJ Jazzy Jeff & the Fresh Prince no fueron a recoger el premio por «Parents Just Don’t Understand»; Kool Moe Dee sí fue, harto de que nadie hablara de estrategia («¿no decíamos que nos importaba un carajo el Grammy?»). En 1990 Young MC lo ganó en directo a «Fight the Power» y Flavor Flav le asaltó el escenario. Eminem fue el primer rapero en ganar un Óscar con «Lose Yourself» (2003, con Luis Resto), y Three 6 Mafia el segundo; Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five entraron los primeros en el Rock and Roll Hall of Fame (2007). En 2014 Macklemore se disculpó con Kendrick Lamar por ganarle; en 2018 DAMN. de Lamar, criado en Top Dawg por Punch, ganó el Pulitzer, algo que Nation of Millions habría merecido treinta años antes.

scenes.name: El hip hop: medio siglo de historia oral
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.desc: Un género nacido de la imaginación de chavales abandonados entre las ruinas del Bronx de los setenta que sobrevivió a todo (a una generación mayor que lo rechazaba, a las radios que no lo ponían, a los políticos que lo atacaban) hasta convertirse en la música más popular de Estados Unidos. Abrams hizo más de trescientas entrevistas entre 2018 y 2022 a DJs, artistas, productores, ejecutivos y periodistas para contar su origen y su expansión: del Bronx a los demás distritos «como las venas de un plano del metro», del parque al vinilo, a la Costa Oeste con el gangsta rap y el G-funk, al Sur y más allá. «La lírica es, al fin y al cabo, una forma de tradición oral.»

facts.title: TacoTron's Jay-Z Hamlet Rap Deep Fake (2022)
facts.body: In the summer of 2022, the text-to-speech program TacoTron generated a rap track using a cloned version of Jay-Z's voice, which recited the "to be or not to be" soliloquy from Shakespeare's Hamlet. This unconventional use of AI to create a deep fake of a well-known musician and post it on YouTube was one of the first widely noted examples and drew strong negative reactions from Jay-Z's representatives. "It wasn't a conventional bit of hip hop. Taco Tron sampled Jay-Z's voice and had it rap the to-be or not to-be solo liquid from Hamlet."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History and Future of AI in Music
facts.name: hip hop

facts.title: Taylor Hawkins' Death (March 25, 2022)
facts.body: Foo Fighters drummer Taylor Hawkins died suddenly on March 25, 2022, in Bogota, Colombia, just before the band was set to headline a festival. At approximately 7:40 PM on that Friday night, a call was made from a Four Seasons property reporting a guest with severe chest pains, but EMS responders arrived too late. Officially, he died from complications related to an enlarged heart (cardiomegaly), which weighed 600 grams (compared to a normal 300 grams). Although his doctors were aware of his enlarged heart for years, attributing it to his active lifestyle of surfing, biking, and intense drumming, little other information regarding his death was released, due to an "airtight" news blackout imposed by the band and management. This lack of information fueled conspiracy theories, though sources suggested a congenital problem exacerbated by exhaustion, as Hawkins had reportedly been feeling "rough" in the months leading up to the South American tour. His death profoundly impacted Dave Grohl, the Foo Fighters, and millions of fans globally. "Taylor was dead. Officially, he died of complications involving an enlarged heart, something called cardiomagalley."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 6: (50-41)
facts.name: Foo Fighters

facts.body: The band embarked on a reunion tour in 2022, which lasted only 36 days, from July 9, 2022, in Troy, Wisconsin, to August 14, 2022, at Madison Square Garden. "Although their reunion lasted all of 36 days before it fell apart, the first show July 9, 2022 in Troy, Wisconsin, last show, August 14, 2022 at Madison Square Garden. It might have gone on longer and might have been much bigger. Ted Singer, Zach D. LaRocca, not torn his Achilles on stage."

facts.title: Tom DeLonge's Return and Reconciliation (2022)
facts.body: By mid-2022, rumors of a reunion circulated, leading to the band's social media accounts being wiped in October. On October 11, the official announcement was made that Tom DeLonge was back, and an album and a two-year world tour were planned. This reconciliation was spurred by Mark Hoppus's cancer diagnosis, which prompted Tom to reach out immediately. "And that's when news came down that Mark, Travis and Tom, came to the realization that it was time to bury all the animosities and get back to being Blink 182."

facts.body: The November 2022 incident involving Taylor Swift concert tickets highlighted the severe impact of ticket buying bots. facts.body: Taylor Hawkins' most recent musical project was NHC, where 'H' stood for Hawkins. The 'N' was Dave Navarro and the 'C' was Chris Cheney, both from Jane's Addiction. facts.title: Death (March 25, 2022)
facts.body: Taylor Hawkins died on Friday, March 25, 2022, in Bogotá, Colombia, at the Four Seasons Casa Medina. An ambulance was called after reports of severe chest pains, but a private doctor could not help, and he was already gone by the time EMS arrived. "Taylor left us. The Fouce fighters were touring South America, and were about to perform at the Estarial picnic in Boca-Tac, Colombia on Friday March 25th, 2022."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Remembering Taylor Hawkins
facts.name: Taylor Hawkins

facts.title: Final Tour Stop and Hotel Stay (March 2022)
facts.body: In March 2022, while on a post-pandemic tour of South America, the Foo Fighters checked into the Four Seasons Casa Medina Hotel in Bogota, Colombia, on Friday, March 25, ahead of their scheduled performance. Taylor Hawkins was reportedly tired, which was not unusual for a touring musician, possibly exacerbated by Bogota's high altitude (over 2600 meters or 8,000 feet) and thin air. "On Friday the 25th of March, the band was scheduled to play in Bogota, Colombia, and had checked into the four seasons Casamadena Hotel in the city's Chapanero district."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

Her husband reported that she passed away "on her own terms, no regrets, she is at peace," with The B-52s song "Rome" playing as she drifted off. "In March 2018, she announced on Facebook that she had systemic lupus and was living in a lot of pain. She found it hard to walk and stand, which sent her into a deep depression. And then she took her own life in a controlled way on June 9, 2022."

facts.title: Black Opry Founder on Country Music's Origins (2022)
facts.body: Holly G, founder of Black Opry, an organization dedicated to promoting Black Country artists, stated in 2022 that black people invented country music and are consistently told it is not for them. She views this as an "American problem," where black people create an art form or industry and are subsequently pushed out of it. "I get told all the time that country music isn't for black people, but the problem is that we invented it."
facts.source: For the Record - The 70s
facts.episode: Ep. 53 - More than Charley Pride - African Americans in 70s Country
facts.name: Holly G

facts.title: Inaugural Convention (2022)
facts.body: Liverpool was chosen to host the first-ever David Bowie World Convention from June 17th to 19th, 2022. This three-day event was held to commemorate the 50th anniversary of Bowie's iconic "Ziggy Stardust" album, bringing together fans for a comprehensive celebration of his work. "Liverpool will host the first ever David Bowie World Convention, three days of all things Bowie, marking the 50th anniversary of the Ziggy Star Test album."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: 60 Mind-Blowing Things About Music: 2021 Edition

facts.title: Chelsea Hotel Room 100 Status (2022)
facts.body: Room 100 of the Chelsea Hotel in New York, where Nancy Spungen was murdered, no longer exists as a distinct room. The hotel ceased being a hotel and was being converted into condos as of early 2022. During a renovation years prior, room 100 was merged with room 103, becoming the bedroom of room 103, and its original entrance door was removed. "As of early 2022, that conversion has been finished. So that's 0.1. 0.2 is that room 100 disappeared long ago."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Infamous Hotels and Hotel Rooms

facts.title: Taylor Hawkins' Last Performance (March 20, 2022)
facts.body: Lollapalooza in Buenos Aires on March 20, 2022, marked Taylor Hawkins' last performance with the Foo Fighters. During this concert, he stepped out from behind the drum kit, as he often did, to sing a song, daring to tackle a Freddie Mercury vocal. "The food fighters at La La Paloza and Buenos Aires. That's Taylor Hawkins last performance."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Remembering Taylor Hawkins

facts.title: Cancelled Performance Due to Taylor Hawkins' Death (March 25, 2022)
facts.body: The Foo Fighters were scheduled to perform at the Estéreo Picnic festival in Bogotá, Colombia, on Friday, March 25, 2022. However, the performance was cancelled due to Taylor Hawkins' death that evening at his hotel. "The Fouce fighters were touring South America, and were about to perform at the Estarial picnic in Boca-Tac, Colombia on Friday March 25th, 2022."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Remembering Taylor Hawkins

facts.title: Taylor Hawkins' Death Circumstances (March 25, 2022)
facts.body: Taylor Hawkins passed away at the Four Seasons Casa Medina in Bogotá, Colombia, on March 25, 2022, following reports of severe chest pains. An ambulance was called, but he was already deceased by the time EMS arrived, after a private doctor was unable to help. "An ambulance was called to the four seasons Casamadena that evening, a guest was reported to be having severe chest pains."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

facts.title: TacoTron's Jay-Z Deep Fake (2022)
facts.body: In the summer of 2022, the text-to-speech program TacoTron generated a rap track that utilized a sampled and cloned version of Jay-Z's voice to rap the "to be or not to be" soliloquy from Shakespeare's Hamlet, which was then posted on YouTube. This incident was one of the first public examples of a "deep fake" of a well-known musician, and Jay-Z's representatives expressed their displeasure. "In the summer of 2022, they generated a rap track that sounded exactly like Jay-Z and posted it on YouTube."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: The History and Future of AI in Music

facts.title: New Zealand Anti-Vax Protest Disruption (2022)
facts.body: In early 2022, New Zealand authorities successfully broke up an anti-vax protest by blasting the crowd with a 15-minute loop mix of Barry Manilow's greatest hits and "Macarena." "And in New Zealand, in early 2022, authorities helped break up an anti-vax protest by blasting the crowd with a mix of Barry Manelow's greatest hits and the Macarena on a 15 minute loop."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
facts.episode: Using Music as a Weapon

facts.title: Kurt Cobain's "Smells Like Teen Spirit" Guitar (2022)
facts.body: The guitar played by Kurt Cobain in Nirvana's iconic "Smells Like Teen Spirit" music video was sold at auction in 2022 for 3.5 million pounds. This highlights the immense value and cultural significance attached to musical instruments featured in landmark music videos. "By the way, the guitar that Kurt used in that video sold it auction in 2022 for 3.5 million pounds."
facts.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
